title: Gradual-exposure DSL: staged promotion, shadow routing, and SLO-aware rollback
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Background:
We need a compact, declarative DSL that lets product and infra teams express staged exposure policies for model promotions and experiments. Current rollout plumbing is fragmented: ad-hoc configs live in multiple services, and guardrails (SLO overrides, automated rollback) require custom orchestration. This ticket defines and implements a first-class Gradual Exposure DSL that covers traffic splits, step schedules, shadow routing, conditional guardrails, and automated rollback policies.

Goals:
- Provide a readable, versionable DSL that compiles to execution plans used by the routing layer.
- Support: staged traffic percentages, pause/windows, shadow traffic (percentage or sample-based), canary metrics bindings (latency/error/quality), and SLO-aware backoff or rollback.
- Emit audit events and linkable run IDs for console traceability.
- Keep runtime footprint small: DSL should compile into a compact JSON plan the router can evaluate with O(1) checks per request.

Non-goals:
- Full A/B experiment analytics platform (this feeds existing analytics; not replacing it).
- Advanced ML quality evaluations (refer to Optimize/evals team).

Proposed DSL (human-friendly example):

exposure_policy: "promo-v1-to-v2"
steps:
  - name: warmup
    duration: 10m
    traffic: 5%
    shadow: 20%   # shadow copies go to v2 but don't affect production responses
    metrics_check:
      - name: p50_latency
        window: 5m
        compare: increase_less_than
        threshold: 20%
    on_failure:
      action: pause
      notify: ["#infra-rollouts","pager"]

  - name: scale
    duration: 30m
    traffic: 25%
    metrics_check:
      - name: error_rate
        window: 10m
        compare: absolute_less_than
        threshold: 0.5%
    on_failure:
      action: rollback
      rollback_window: 15m
      notify: ["#infra-rollouts"]

  - name: final
    duration: 1h
    traffic: 100%
    baselines:
      - name: model_quality
        source: "pset/regression-suite/latest"

Guardrails and semantics:
- metrics_check binds to the metrics service (Grafana/Prometheus) via stable metric IDs. The DSL supports both relative (percent) and absolute thresholds.
- on_failure actions: pause | rollback | backoff (reduce increment) | alert. Backoff reduces next step traffic by a defined factor.
- Shadowing: can be percentage or deterministic sampling key. Shadow traffic must be explicitly opt-in per step.
- Audit: every state transition must emit an event with rollout_id + step + actor + evidence links.

Acceptance criteria (internal):
1) DSL parser implemented in redwood/rollout (golang) with unit tests covering parser, validation, and compile -> plan translation (>=90% coverage).
2) Router accepts compiled plan and executes staged changes in the staging environment with simulated traffic.
3) Automated metrics checks: wire up Prometheus query interface with mocks for CI; ensure on_failure actions trigger the expected state transitions.
4) Console: rollout trace view shows step timestamps, emitted audit events, and links to the Prometheus queries used.
5) Security: DSL validation rejects any policy that would route customer PII to non-approved targets; documented in runtime-1.23 security checklist.

Open design decisions / trade-offs:
- Language surface: YAML-like vs JSON-first. We prefer YAML for author ergonomics but compile to compact JSON for the router.
- Expressivity vs safety: allowing arbitrary PromQL could give power but increase risk; we will support a restricted query template with whitelisted metrics.
- Where to store policies: git-backed repo (recommended) vs in-console editor. Plan: policies canonicalized in repo for audit; console provides a view and a gated apply flow.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: DSL schema + parser + compile to json-plan (ENG-45711-branch).
- Week 2: integrate compile step in rollout service; add unit tests and small e2e harness.
- Week 3: metrics binding + mock metrics server for CI tests.
- Week 4: Console trace UI + audit event integration; security review.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Gradual+Exposure+DSL
- Draft schema proto: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/rollout-dsl-schema (internal)
- PR (parser scaffold): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1723
- Grafana samples: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/rollout-traces

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: False positives from noisy metrics causing rollbacks. Mitigation: require two consecutive failing windows for auto-rollback, and provide a manual override labeled as operator-rollback with justification.
- Risk: Too many policy variants increases cognitive load. Mitigation: ship with 3 curated templates (canary, ramp, shadow-only) and expand later.

Note: This ticket touches runtime routing, console, and metrics teams. Expect cross-team review; please coordinate with @Nina Patel (console PM) and @Ravi Singh (observability).
